mechanism: %PARSE-KEY-PATH (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:203-213) signals "Multipath descriptors are not supported" for ANY path element of the form <...> when multipath IS allowed (:211), and Core's own "specifies multipath in a section where multipath is not allowed" when it is not (:212). Every consumer that reaches PARSE-DESCRIPTOR (descriptors.lisp:1032) therefore refuses BIP389: getdescriptorinfo (descriptors.lisp:2060ff), scantxoutset via descriptor-scanobject-scripts, generatetodescriptor/generateblock via parse-output-descriptor, descriptorprocesspsbt (src/wallet/psbt.lisp:1565) and the send/fund solving_data path (src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:2860). Only TWO shipped entry points expand first: importdescriptors (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2173, %PROCESS-DESCRIPTOR-IMPORT) and deriveaddresses (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:2089), both through EXPAND-MULTIPATH-DESCRIPTOR. Core does the expansion inside the parser -- ParseKeyPath expands the specifier and Parse() returns a VECTOR of descriptors (refs/bitcoin/src/script/descriptor.cpp:1789-1851) -- so every Core consumer gets it for free, and getdescriptorinfo additionally emits a multipath_expansion array when descs.size() > 1 (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/output_script.cpp:206-213). We have no such field. Refuter checks that FAILED to refute it: (1) the rejection is not a checksum or network artefact -- the identical string with a valid checksum is accepted by deriveaddresses and importdescriptors in the same image and node; (2) it is not confined to an exotic shape -- a plain single-specifier wpkh(tpub/<0;1>/*), the canonical BIP389 form every wallet exports, is the case that fails; (3) the documented scoping decision is STALE, not merely narrow: tests/wallet/descriptor-tests.lisp:223 (desc-core-multipath-rejected) and the file header at src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:21 both say multipath is out of scope, while src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2155-2177 and src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:2084-2101 implement it, the latter's own comment noting that "deriveaddresses went on refusing multipath outright" and fixing exactly that one caller. Nothing in docs/ or in a test records the consequence that remains.
consequence: S2: getdescriptorinfo -- Core's documented way to validate and canonicalise a descriptor before importing it -- answers RPC -5 "Multipath descriptors are not supported" for a descriptor that Core accepts and that OUR OWN importdescriptors imports successfully in the same session. An operator or a wallet tool that gates on getdescriptorinfo concludes a valid export is malformed and never attempts the import that would have worked. scantxoutset (the balance-check path for an unimported descriptor), descriptorprocesspsbt (the offline-signer path) and generatetodescriptor cannot be pointed at a BIP389 descriptor at all, with no in-node workaround other than hand-expanding the string into its /0/* and /1/* forms. No funds are stuck: importdescriptors and deriveaddresses both work on the single-specifier form, so a wallet CAN be set up from the export; what is lost is validation, scanning and PSBT processing, plus the multipath_expansion field Core reports. The scoping decision in desc-core-multipath-rejected is not a defence -- its "P0 scope" claim is contradicted by two shipped code paths, and the resulting inconsistency (one RPC calls invalid what another accepts) is recorded nowhere.

fix_shape: Move the expansion into the parser, where Core has it, instead of adding a third caller of the string expander. Give %PARSE-KEY-PATH Core's ParseKeyPath contract (descriptor.cpp:1789-1851): when allow_multipath and it meets a <a;b;...> element it records ONE placeholder plus the substitute values (rejecting a second specifier in the same key expression, fewer than two values, and duplicates -- all three messages already exist in %MULTIPATH-SUBSTITUTES) and returns a LIST of key paths rather than one; a key expression then yields a vector of desc-keys. %PARSE-DESCRIPTOR-BODY collects one vector per key expression, clones length-1 vectors up to max_providers_len and errors "<fn>(): Multipath derivation paths have mismatched lengths" otherwise (descriptor.cpp:2368-2384), and PARSE-DESCRIPTOR returns a LIST of out-descs. Keep a single-descriptor accessor for the many callers that legitimately want one (Core's descs.at(0)), and then wire the consumers Core wires: getdescriptorinfo reports descs.at(0) plus a multipath_expansion array when there is more than one (output_script.cpp:206-213); deriveaddresses returns one address array per expansion (it already does, via the string expander -- switch it to the parsed vector); scantxoutset, descriptorprocesspsbt and the solving_data path iterate the expansions. importdescriptors keeps its own rule that with exactly two expansions the second IS the internal chain (backup.cpp:227-233), which %PROCESS-MULTIPATH-IMPORT already implements. Delete EXPAND-MULTIPATH-DESCRIPTOR once the parser owns it -- it is the source of c9da9f50 as well. Rewrite tests/wallet/descriptor-tests.lisp:223 from a rejection assertion into Core's CheckMultipath vectors (descriptor_tests.cpp:748, :803), and update the stale scope note at src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:21.
